cards.body: For the first time in its 33-year history, Nvidia on Tuesday reported quarterly financial results without Jensen Huang at its helm or on the call, after its cofounder and longtime chief executive departed five days ago . To no one's surprise, Nvidia continues to set new financial records as demand for its AI accelerators shows no signs of slowing down. The company reported revenue of $115.8 billion for the third quarter of its fiscal 2027, with its latest Vera Rubin platform generating $20 billion. Meanwhile, its supply commitments surged to $390 billion. 'Momentum is real' "Our momentum is real. NVIDIA is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people," said Colette Kress, interim chief executive and chief financial officer of Nvidia. "Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track, and our ambition has never been greater." For the third quarter of fiscal 2027, which ended on October 25, 2026, Nvidia posted revenue of $115.844 billion, an increase of 20% sequentially and 103% year-over-year. The company's net income reached $65.287 billion, up 105% from the same quarter last year, while gross margin hit 74.8%. Revenue from the Compute & Networking segment totaled $106 billion, up 20% quarter-over-quarter and 108% year-over-year. Meanwhile, the Graphics segment generated $9.8 billion, a sequential increase of 25% and 62% compared with the same period a year ago. (Image credit: Nvidia) As expected, Nvidia's results during the quarter were primarily driven by its Data Center business, which generated $107.6 billion in revenue (and accounted for approximately 93% of the company's sales), up 21% sequentially and 110% YoY. Hyperscale customers accounted for $60.1 billion, an increase of 23% QoQ and 71% YoY, while sales to AI Clouds, Industrial & Enterprise customers reached $47.5 billion, up 18% sequentially and 195% compared to the same period last year. Although hyperscalers remain Nvidia's largest customer category, demand from AI cloud providers, industrial companies, and enterprises continues to grow considerably faster on an annual basis. Meanwhile, Edge Computing revenue reached $8.2 billion, up 14% sequentially and 42% year-over-year. (Image credit: Nvidia) One of the main contributors to Nvidia's growth was its Vera Rubin platform, which generated nearly $20 billion in revenue in its first quarter of production shipments, which Nvidia described as the fastest product ramp in its history. The company also reported strong demand for standalone Vera CPUs and continued sales growth for Blackwell Ultra. According to Nvidia, its hyperscale partners brought Vera Rubin systems into production in approximately one month, which is two times faster than the previous-generation Grace Blackwell platform. cards.body: Five days after Nvidia's Jensen Huang resigned from the company he co-founded 33 years ago under a cloud of scandal, a nervous base of shareholders eagerly awaited Colette Kress' first public appearance as interim CEO. Following Nvidia's better-than-expected earnings report on Tuesday, Kress offered some relief to Wall Street, at least temporarily, by proclaiming on the call with analysts that customers are still fully onboard and that there's no slippage in demand. She said leadership from Nvidia's most important supplier, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, visited company offices this week. "We've engaged with our customers, we've engaged with our suppliers, our partners, they're all 100% behind us," Kress said on the call. "Customers have expressed their support to the business outlook and helping us through that." While Huang was a singular figure in artificial intelligence with a commanding presence across the globe, Nvidia is still at the center of the AI ecosystem. Customers ranging from hyperscalers and neoclouds to frontier labs like OpenAI and Anthropic remain in persistent need of its technology and capital. Nvidia shares climbed almost 5% in extended trading on Tuesday after the chipmaker's better-than-expected earnings and strong guidance. That still leaves the stock in a deep slump after a 24% drop so far this month, driven by broad concerns about a slowdown in the AI buildout, a political handoff in Washington, D.C., and the turmoil at the top of the company. Despite all those headwinds and what Nvidia called the "unexpected transition" in leadership, the business is still booming. Revenue more than doubled in the latest quarter to $115.84 billion, and Nvidia projects roughly 90% growth in the current period to about $130 billion. More importantly, Kress said the 70% growth forecast for next year that was offered over the summer is actually too low. Now the projection is 75%. That's for a company that's seen revenue multiply by about 15-fold since the launch of ChatGPT in late 2022. While Huang is gone, "demand did not leave with him," Yorkville Ives analyst Dan Ives said in a note after the report. Kress maintained her optimistic tone in an interview with CNBC's Jim Cramer after the call. "The most important thing that we have been seeing is continuing growth in terms of the demand that's out there," she said. Looking to the future Kress also said on the call that Nvidia's stepped-up buybacks, announced in September, are still on track, confirming that the board had added $150 billion to the company's authorization for share repurchases. It's not all on Kress. The consistent message throughout the earnings call was that Nvidia is preparing for life after Huang. The updated regulation now requires licenses for renting those chips in large quantities to the entirety of America's D:5 countries list (nations embargoed from arms sales). As expected, the news landed in Beijing like a lead dragon, and its Ministry of Commerce states that China "will take countermeasures to firmly safeguard national sovereignty, security, and development interests." Both nations were recently embroiled in a bitter trade war, with ever-mounting tariffs and restrictions on both sides until a temporary truce was called in Oct. 2025. Only some restrictions were lifted, though; for example, Chinese semiconductors still face a 50% tariff when imported stateside. A potential restart of tariff-slapping would all but guarantee an even larger amount of turmoil in U.S. stock markets. Nvidia cut off about half of its Asian buyers last July, seemingly in the purview of the export controls, and told data center operators that over 50% of their business must come from non-Chinese companies. Meanwhile, both Malaysia and Singapore have intensified their scrutiny of AI hardware shipments. China's countermeasures ammo is as of yet unspecified. The nation had restricted the sale of gallium, germanium, and antimony to the U.S. previously, and the truce shelved that bullet until Nov. 2027. Beijing may well choose to simply not renew that agreement when that day comes. Although analysts believe that the nations will be cordial enough during this summit, Trump's perceived provocation may bring China's proverbial nuclear option of restricting rare earth exports back to the loading bay. cards.body: AI 추천 뉴스 엔비디아 "투자 기업 엄격히 심사"…'AI 중앙은행' 역할 축소하나 분기매출 1158억弗 '역대 최대'…홀로서기 본격화 구매약정 3900억弗로 40% 늘어 삼전닉스 수년치 HBM 일감 확보 젠슨 황 추진한 순환거래는 '제동' 네오클라우드 지원 까다로워질듯 한국경제신문의 투자 전문 유료 플랫폼 '한경 프리미엄9'에 실린 기사입니다. 한경 프리미엄9(www.hankyung.com/premium9)을 구독하시면 더 많은 글로벌 투자 기사를 찾아볼 수 있습니다. “젠슨 황은 떠났지만 인공지능(AI) 수요는 떠나지 않았다.” 17일(현지시간) 젠슨 황 없이 처음 이뤄진 엔비디아 분기 실적발표에 대한 기술 투자자 댄 아이브스의 평가다. 콜렛 크레스 임시 최고경영자(CEO)는 그간 젠슨 황이 추진한 인공지능(AI) 인프라 기업에 대한 순환거래(벤더파이낸싱) 축소를 시사하면서도 매출 증가율 예상치는 더 높였다. ‘가죽 재킷’을 벗은 엔비디아의 홀로서기가 본격화했다는 분석이 나온다. ◇젠슨 황 없이도 순항 엔비디아는 이날 2027회계연도 3분기(2026년 8~10월) 시장 추정치를 웃도는 실적을 발표하면서 2028회계연도(2027년 2월~2028년 1월) 매출 증가율 전망을 전 분기 70%에서 75%로 상향 조정했다. 크레스 CEO는 “직전 분기 매출 증가율 추정이 70%로 제한된 이유가 공급망 한계 때문”이라며 “이번엔 고객에게 추가로 공급 가능한 물량을 반영했다”고 설명했다. 중국 데이터센터 매출은 포함되지 않은 수치다. 차세대 그래픽처리장치(GPU) 베라루빈의 출시 효과도 본격화했다. 기존 블랙웰을 잇는 AI 칩 베라루빈은 이번 분기에 본격 출하됐다. 크레스 CEO는 “베라루빈은 폭발적인 출발을 보이고 있다”며 “우리의 야심은 그 어느 때보다 크다”고 밝혔다. 베라루빈 등 제조에 필요한 부품 구매는 늘렸다. 엔비디아의 이번 분기 필수 부품·생산 역량 구매약정은 3900억달러로 전 분기(2790억달러)보다 40% 늘었다. 다년간의 메모리 장기공급계약(LTA)을 맺은 영향이다. 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스가 수년간의 HBM 일감을 상당 수준 확보했다는 해석이 나온다. 베라루빈에는 두 회사가 공급하는 HBM4(6세대)와 저전력 메모리 모듈인 ‘소캠(SOCAMM) 2’가 적용된다. 업계 관계자는 “젠슨 황 스캔들 등으로 최근 AI 투자 축소 우려가 불거졌지만 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스의 메모리를 원하는 기업은 여전히 많다”며 “대외 정책 불확실성으로 AI 투자 증가세가 일부 둔화할 가능성은 있지만 당분간 업황이 뒤바뀔 가능성은 크지 않다”고 내다봤다. 엔비디아의 다른 공급사도 한숨을 돌리게 됐다. 삼성전기는 엔비디아와 반도체 기판 관련 추가 계약을 맺었으며 엔비디아가 추가 자금 지원을 검토 중이라고 이날 밝혔다. ◇“미래 투자, 보증 엄격히 평가” 막대한 현금흐름을 바탕으로 AI 생태계에 자금을 지원해온 엔비디아의 ‘중앙은행’ 역할은 축소될 가능성이 크다. 크레스 CEO는 AI 인프라 투자와 관련해 “시장이 성숙해지고 추가 자본 조달원이 확보됨에 따라 미래 투자와 약정, 보증을 더욱 엄격히 평가하겠다”고 밝혔다. 젠슨 황이 회사 현금흐름을 다시 고객사에 투자하는 순환거래를 통해 어느 정도 AI 생태계를 구축해놓은 만큼 이제 그 역할을 줄이겠다는 뜻으로 해석된다. 이에 따라 엔비디아 GPU를 구매해 임대하는 인프라 사업자 네오클라우드 지원은 더욱 까다로워질 것으로 전망된다. 크레스 CEO는 “전력과 토지, 건물을 확보한 네오클라우드에 자금을 최우선 지원하겠다”고 했다. 기반 시설이 없는 네오클라우드는 지원 대상에서 제외하겠다는 의미로 풀이된다. 또 신용등급이 투기등급(BB) 이하인 네오클라우드는 고객과 실제로 컴퓨팅 자원 판매·임대 계약을 맺었는지 보기로 했다. 이는 일부 네오클라우드가 자금 조달에 어려움을 겪으며 경영 위기에 처한 상황과 맞물린다. 일론 머스크 테슬라 CEO는 지난달 네오클라우드를 관상어인 구피에 빗대며 “200개 넘는 기업이 폐사할 것”이라고 경고했다. 시장에서는 크레스 CEO가 젠슨 황이 확대해놓은 AI 생태계 투자를 다시 줄이는 ‘회계 다이어트’에 들어갔다는 분석이 나온다. 재무통인 크레스 CEO는 순환금융 규모가 지나치게 커지는 데 대해 반대했던 것으로 알려졌다. 실리콘밸리=김인엽 특파원/노유정 기자 inside@hankyung.com

cards.body: 독일 피지컬 인공지능(AI) 기업 애자일 로봇(Agile Robots)이 소프트뱅크와 엔비디아 등이 참여한 투자 라운드에서 5억달러(약 7300억원)를 조달했다. 이번 투자에서 인정받은 기업가치는 85억달러(약 12조4000억원) 규모다. 이번 시리즈 F 투자 라운드는 소프트뱅크 그룹이 주도했으며 엔비디아, 히타치 그룹, T.캐피탈 등이 참여했다. 이번 투자로 애자일 로봇의 누적 투자 유치액은 20억달러로 늘었다. 2018년 독일 항공우주센터(DLR)에서 분사해 설립된 애자일 로봇은 독일 뮌헨에 본사를 두고 있다. 휴머노이드와 이동형 로봇, 로봇 팔과 손을 비롯해 관련 소프트웨어와 AI 모델을 개발하는 기업이다. 물류와 자동차, 전자, 제조업 등에서 사람의 숙련된 작업과 판단이 필요한 공정을 자동화하는 데 주력하고 있다. 애자일 로봇은 이번 투자금을 미국 시장 확대와 로봇 기술 개발, 생산시설 확충 등에 투입할 계획이다. 독일 내 생산 역량도 강화하고 있다. 올해 초 뮌헨 인근 퓌르스텐펠트브루크에 구축한 생산시설은 다리형 및 바퀴형 휴머노이드 로봇을 연간 최대 1만대 생산할 수 있는 규모다. 자오펑 첸 애자일 로봇 최고경영자(CEO)는 “피지컬 AI는 세상이 제품을 만들고 이동시키는 방식을 근본적으로 바꿀 것”이라며 “이번 투자를 통해 글로벌 사업 확장을 앞당기고 주요 시장에서 입지를 강화하는 동시에 생산 능력을 확대할 수 있게 됐다”고 말했다. 데니스 창 소프트뱅크 인베스트먼트 어드바이저스 매니징 파트너는 “피지컬 AI가 산업 전반을 변화시킬 것으로 보고 있다”며 “애자일 로봇은 로봇 공학 전문성과 산업 현장에 기술을 적용하는 역량을 결합해 피지컬 AI의 상용화를 이끌고 있다”고 말했다. 한재희 기자 onej@chosunbiz.com

cards.body: New U.S. export rules could slow Southeast Asia's data center boom by tightening access to advanced AI chips and targeting the region's role in providing computing power to Chinese companies. According to an interim rule released Monday by the Commerce Department, data centers in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia will need a U.S. government license to purchase advanced AI chips, including those from Nvidia. Facilities already serving large Chinese customers will have 90 days to apply for a license or face future export restrictions, the rule said. The region has seen a surge in data center construction to house the semiconductors needed to train and develop artificial intelligence models. U.S. restrictions on China's access to Nvidia's most advanced chips have pushed Chinese technology firms, including Alibaba Group and ByteDance, to rent computing capacity in overseas data centers. About 75% of China's overseas AI compute was forecast to be concentrated in Southeast Asia by the end of 2026, according to October estimates by the Institute for Progress, a Washington-based think tank. The buildout has come under greater scrutiny as Washington presses ahead with the investigation into Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang. Huang left the company that he co-founded in 1993 after reports of several alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy who is believed to facilitate billions of dollars worth of Nvidia chips into China. The new restrictions will likely make building and operating these data centers "slower and costlier," said Jessica Brandt, a senior fellow for technology and national security at the Council on Foreign Relations. The rules could undercut the business model of neoclouds — newer cloud providers built around AI computing — in the region, she said. Operators are likely to face more rigorous regulatory and national security requirements, said Reema Bhattacharya, head of Asia research at risk intelligence company Verisk Maplecroft. Greater scrutiny over investment into these projects could also weigh on Asian economies that have benefited heavily from the region's data center build-out. Who are most exposed? Malaysia stands to lose the most from the new restrictions, analysts say, given the scale of capacity being built in Johor and the sector's reliance on Chinese customers. More than half of Malaysia's data center capacity is in colocation facilities with Chinese firms accounting for "a sizeable share of these workloads," said Leah Fahy, senior China economist at Capital Economics. Restricting access to overseas cloud facilities would weaken the commercial case for further expansion and ultimately weigh on investment from both Chinese and U.S. companies, Fahy said. "Any resulting slowdown in investment would add to the drag from an anticipated cooling in the global AI export cycle," she said, potentially knocking 0.2 percentage points off Malaysia's GDP growth forecasts through 2028. summary_data.subject_angle: **Nvidia는 사상 최대 수준의 데이터센터 수요(Q3·Q4 가이던스 모두 서프라이즈)를 입증했지만, CEO 교체 불확실성과 의회·수출규제 대응이라는 비사업적 리스크가 주가와 투자자 신뢰에 직접 영향을 미치는 국면에 들어섰다.** interim CEO Kress는 hyperscaler 수요가 견고하다고 강조하며 고객 다변화로 리스크를 방어하는 메시지를 내고 있다.

cards.body: Nvidia shares declined another 2.89% Wednesday after the company issued its first earnings report since the departure of former CEO Jensen Huang. The stock is down more than 13% over the past week. Trading in the neocloud companies was volatile throughout the day, as CoreWeave closed down 4.13%, Iren sank 3.61% and Nebius whipsawed, ending the trading day up 0.87%. Nvidia's third-quarter revenue came in at $115.84 billion, more than $6 billion above analysts' expectations of $109.10 billion, while fourth-quarter guidance of $130 billion topped the $125.1 billion consensus, according to LSEG. The semiconductor giant continues to navigate the fallout from Huang's resignation last week. Shortly before the results, Huang made his first public statement since resigning last week, saying that he was open to returning to the company, after an outpouring of support from prominent tech figures. But Harvey Jones, the new and first-ever chair of Nvidia's board, said on the earnings call that the board does not intend to reinstate him as CEO. ″[Hyperscalers] are the ones that are right now feverishly looking for more focus in terms of the compute that we have available," interim CEO Colette Kress told Jim Cramer on CNBC's "Mad Money." "This concept that anything is changing in terms of any of our types of customers — that is just not true. They are all continuing to be with us, and we have a very deep breath of different customers." The U.S. Commerce Department announced a legal change on Monday to try and stem China's access to the most advanced Nvidia chips — which are already under export controls effectively preventing their import into the country — by restricting Chinese companies' ability to access compute remotely in overseas data centers. In a letter Wednesday, the House Energy and Commerce Committee asked Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to appear to discuss chip export controls, and requested a briefing from interim CEO Colette Kress by Dec. 2. Nvidia told investors in its earnings commentary that it was "not assuming any Data Center compute revenue from China in our outlook," in keeping with its recent language on the country. Huang is slated to appear before several Congressional committees in the coming weeks. Speaking to CNBC's "Squawk Box" Wednesday, Senate Banking Committee Chair Tim Scott, R-S.C., said Huang and Lutnick have agreed to appear before the committee in December. It's slated to be Huang's second appearance on Capitol Hill in December, after the former Nvidia CEO reached an agreement with three House committees to appear for closed-door interviews on Dec. 1. — CNBC's Caleigh Keating contributed to this report.

cards.body: China's People's Liberation Army has been "actively soliciting" Nvidia's most advanced semiconductor chips to develop its artificial intelligence-enabled military capabilities, a congressional commission said in a report released Wednesday. The report comes as Nvidia has been rocked by the resignation of its CEO, Jensen Huang, after reports that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy who worked for Singapore-based Megaspeed, which is being eyed by U.S. investigators for potential diversion of Nvidia's chips to China. "China is seeking to evade U.S. export controls to gain the most advanced semiconductors that underpin its intelligentization drive," the U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission said in its 2026 annual report to Congress. China is making that move as it faces a quality gap between chips produced by Chinese companies, including Huawei and Cambricon, and the more advanced ones produced by Nvidia and other U.S. companies, such as Advanced Micro Devices, the report noted. The report's findings could fuel concerns about advanced Nvidia chips having found their way to Chinese users amid escalating investigations from Congress and state and federal regulators. "Although China has made some progress in achieving its goals, it has not yet closed the hardest chokepoints — including the most advanced capabilities in logic fabrication, memory, and semiconductor manufacturing equipment, as well as the Nvidia Compute Unified Device Architecture (CUDA) software moat — and likely will not for some time," the report said. "The resulting gap in compute is substantial, largely due to U.S. export controls on advanced chips," the report said. The report highlighted the fact that in the meantime, Chinese companies have obtained remote access to Nvidia chips through data centers in third countries, including Malaysia. On Tuesday, the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security issued a rule intended to cut off that workaround. The move came in response to criticism from Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Congress members that the Commerce Department had not done enough to prevent Nvidia's most advanced chips from being diverted to China in violation of U.S. export controls. The U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission was created by Congress in 2000 with a mandate to monitor and report to Congress the national security implications of the trade and economic relationship between the U.S. and China.

headlines.body: One reason 197,000 people, including Elon Musk, signed a petition over the weekend calling on Nvidia to reinstate the company’s ousted CEO Jensen Huang is that he wasn’t just championing the AI boom. He was using Nvidia’s enormous profits to help finance it. And Nvidia has a lot of money to spend. The company reported on Tuesday net income of $64.9 billion for the third quarter, which was up from $59.7 billion the prior quarter. But Nvidia’s continued success depends on having enough customers building and expanding data centers to keep buying its AI chips and systems. Under Huang, the company aggressively invested in AI startups and neoclouds and, more recently, began guaranteeing massive loans to finance new data centers. The biggest deal yet was the $105 billion backstop for OpenAI’s PORTS-Pike data center campus in Ohio, announced in August. In exchange for that loan guarantee, OpenAI promised that the campus would exclusively use Nvidia’s equipment, the company said. Huang’s abrupt departure last week raised questions about whether Nvidia would continue bankrolling its customers at the same pace. There were reports that CFO Colette Kress, now interim CEO, had tried to push back on Huang’s increasingly ambitious dealmaking. She reportedly reduced the backstop guarantee for the OpenAI project from $250 billion down to $105 billion. Under Kress, Nvidia clarified in its quarterly CFO commentary that guaranteeing a loan doesn’t mean the company is providing the financing itself. The guarantee only takes effect once the customer has secured the financing needed to build the facility and install Nvidia’s products. If the project fails to meet those conditions, the guarantee “doesn’t exist” she said. “There is the raising of capital that they may need through equity and or debt, in order to build out any of the buildings, get them ready for use, but also the ability to procure the compute, install the compute, and get ready. What we are indicating in our statement there is that is when our guarantee starts. So if all of that begins and unfortunately they are delayed or they have a challenge in terms of building that, our guarantee doesn’t exist anymore,” Kress said to analysts on Tuesday during the quarterly conference call. She pointed to OpenAI PORTS-Pike campus as an example of where such terms apply. When asked, she also said this wasn’t a change in policy, but simply a clarification of existing terms. However, these disclosures have never been public before. Kress also made clear that Nvidia wasn’t bailing on all the ways it was financing the AI boom, especially new data centers. But, she said, Nvidia was going to be far more selective in the future. “The availability of land, power, shell is such a critical part of the whole structure in terms of building out those data centers. headlines.body: Even though Nvidia says that it does not plan to bring its former CEO Jensen Huang back to the company, that hasn't stopped some of its board members from continuing to lobby for his return. Following the news that some of Huang's allies have formed a "war room" to drive his reinstatement just days after his resignation, one Nvidia employee went so far as to warn that the company faces the possibility of an exodus of "irreplaceable talent" if Huang isn't reinstated. We've even seen U.S. President Trump argue for giving Huang his old job back , but the company said during its November 17 earnings call that wasn't in the cards. Now, Semafor reports that some Nvidia board members aren't taking "no" for an answer. Huang, for his part, has already said that he would be "honored" to return to the company that he resigned from in disgrace just a few days ago . At the time, he admitted to having an affair with a woman who worked for Megaspeed, a controversial Nvidia customer linked to the smuggling of export-controlled AI hardware into China. That woman has also been accused of being a Chinese spy, further complicating an already troublesome matter for Nvidia and Huang. Huang and Nvidia's top lawyer will make an appearance before the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence, and China Select Committees in early December and are likely to face some difficult questions. But despite all of this, Huang is said to have spoken with at least one Nvidia board member about the possibility of making a return to Nvidia. That meeting took place hours before Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said on the company’s earnings call that Huang wasn't coming back. The board voted unanimously to accept his resignation, and won't be backtracking. It's reported that three board members don't agree with that stance, while others have already turned their attention to who will replace Huang long-term. Interim CEO Colette Kress is not being considered as a full-time replacement for Huang. Instead, Arm CEO Rene Haas has appeared as a frontrunner for the top job, with the Nvidia board believed to have already made an approach. Marvell CEO Matt Murphy is also another name under consideration, but the ongoing calls for Huang to be brought back into the fold are thought to have put him off. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney have also chimed in , while a Taiwanese skyscraper was used to send messages of support to a man who has proven hugely popular in the country.

headlines.body: Democrats are scrutinizing the business of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's adult sons as they investigate why the top Trump administration official allegedly resisted cracking down on companies suspected of diverting Nvidia's advanced AI chips to China. The probe unveiled Wednesday ratchets up the pressure Lutnick was already facing from inside and outside the Trump administration. It provides the latest sign that Nvidia, the scandal-scarred AI behemoth, will be embroiled in congressional Democrats' coming anti-corruption crusade, as well as a wider bipartisan effort to clamp down on AI chip sales to China. Reps. Jamie Raskin, D-Md., and Gregory Meeks, D-N.Y., the respective ranking members of the House Judiciary and Foreign Affairs Committees, are demanding reams of records from Cantor Fitzgerald, the investment firm Brandon and Kyle Lutnick took over from their father after he joined President Donald Trump's Cabinet in February 2025. "We seek to understand whether any actions or decisions by Secretary Lutnick concerning export controls, enforcement measures, or national security policies may have been improperly influenced by Cantor Fitzgerald's holdings or business interests," the Democrats wrote in a letter sent Tuesday to Brandon Lutnick. At the time of Howard Lutnick's confirmation, Cantor had amassed a stake in Nvidia reportedly valued around $1.2 billion, one of its largest holdings for its clients. Between September 2025 and March 2026, the firm reported a nearly 50% decline in its Nvidia holdings, a CNBC analysis of securities filings found. In the same time period, Lutnick had reportedly been pressed to take action against Megaspeed, a Singapore-based tech firm accused of transferring Nvidia AI chips to China. The New York Times reported in October 2025 that the Commerce Department was investigating Megaspeed's ties to Beijing. Lutnick "repeatedly stood in the way" of implementing controls on Megaspeed and other companies suspected of funneling cutting-edge chips to China, Axios reported Nov. 11. "Secretary Lutnick's reported obstruction may have resulted in billions of dollars of restricted AI chips being diverted to China," read the Democrats' letter, which was also signed by Rep. Sydney Kamlager-Dove, D-Calif., the ranking member of the Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on South and Central Asia. Lutnick's reported dithering may also have propped up Nvidia share prices for months, "preventing devastating losses for your company," the Democrats wrote. headlines.body: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee, panel Chair Tim Scott, R-S.C., said on CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Wednesday. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has also agreed to testify, Scott said. The agreements to appear voluntarily come as pressure builds on Capitol Hill to investigate Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy, which led to his ouster at the chipmaker he founded. "They both have agreed," Scott said. "We will hopefully have this done before Christmas." Huang reached an agreement on Tuesday with the chairmen of three House committees for a closed-door transcribed interview on Dec. 1 jointly before the three panels. Scott had asked Huang to appear publicly in the Senate. A spokesperson for the banking committee did not immediately respond to questions about when Huang and Lutnick would testify. In initial letters to the pair, Scott requested Huang appear on Dec. 3 and Lutnick appear on Dec. 10. "Nvidia seemed to have fairly lax controls, and I want to know how much of the relationship with Alice [Huang] impacted Nvidia's unwillingness or inability, or frankly, just blindness to Megaspeed's providing access to China of the most advanced chipset," Scott said of Jensen Huang's testimony. The details of Huang's appearance before the three House panels on Dec. 1 are still being determined, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Rep. Brian Mast, R-Fla., told reporters at the Capitol on Wednesday. He said the people who will likely conduct the closed-door interview will be the top Republican and top Democrat on his panel and the Select Committee on China and Select Committee on Intelligence along with their attorneys. The location is still being worked out, Mast said. A date for an appearance before the committees by Jeffrey Kessler, the Commerce official who oversees export controls, is not yet set, Mast said. Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter is scheduled to appear before the panels Dec. 2. Scott, in his CNBC appearance, also homed in on Lutnick, calling for answers as to why the commerce secretary did not act after being warned about Megaspeed — the Singaporean company where the alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang, was an executive. Nvidia sold its chips to Megaspeed, which U.S. investigators suspect of diverting them to China. "They were warned as early as March of this year, several months ago, that Megaspeed should be on the 'entity list,'" Scott said, referring to a Commerce Department list of companies the U.S. views as national security risks. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security "didn't do it, Howard didn't do it, we want to know why." Lutnick and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have been embroiled in an intra-administration battle as the fallout from the Huang affair grows.
